(A) According to you which amino acid is most suitable for each position (among the given  
  options - Tryptophan, Threonine, Glutamine) and why?  
  You can submit your answer by filling the table  
  
  
  (B) What is the type of protein structure is visible at point D?  
  (C) Mr Keerthan replaced all the lysine with glycine before submitting to his professor. Will that  
  protein be still be functional? Justify.

  He informed his professor and he says that it can't be reversed once lost the protein structure.  
  Based on your understanding give a proper justification.

2A)    Predict the outcome of the cross in the following:  
  Tall Round (TtRr) X dwarf wrinkled (ttrr)                                                           (3)  
  Calculate phenotypic and genotypic ratio  
  
2B)    How Morgan was able to prove that the factor for eye colour is located on X chromosome.  
  Logically explain.                                                                                  (3)  
  
2C)                                                                                                        (4)

Identify the most probable mode of inheritance in (a) and (b). Justify.  
  
  
  What is the probability of a male being affected for an affected father in this mode of inheritance  
  (a) and (b)?  
  
3A)   A RNA polymerase is involved in transcribing a DNA segment (given below). If the polymerase  
  transcribes this sequence from left to right, what will the sequence of RNA be? What will the  
  RNA sequence be if the polymerase moves right to left? For the both the cases what would be the  
  template strand.                                                                                (3)  
  
  
3B)   A group of students wanted to repeat the experiments conducted by Meselson-Stahl. The bacteria  
  was grown initially in the heavy nitrogen media and then shifted to lighter nitrogen media. The  
  students conducted density gradient centrifugation to deduce the mode of replication of this  
  newly found bacteria. What mode of replication does this bacteria follow ?  
  How will you logically rule out other modes of replication here?  
  $$L = Light strand 14N and H= Heavy strand 15N$$  
  
  
  (3)  
  
  
  (1+2 = 3 marks)  
  
3C)   DNA sequence shown below is of a gene (only one strand sequence been given) that encodes a  
  short peptide. Peptide sequence is also given below. Based on the information given answer the  
  following question.  
  3'-TCGA GTAC ACG CTC AGG ACT GCG ACT GATCC-5'  
  (4)  
  i) Give the mature mRNA sequence of the gene with proper labels - newly formed and mature.  
  ii) Justify why only 4 amino acid are synthesized from 31 nucleotides?  
  (2+1 = 3 marks)  
  
4A)   (i) Hummingbirds feed on nectar from flowers. The flowers are pollinated by hummingbirds as  
  they move from flower to flower. What type of interaction is seen in this?  
  (ii) Biofilms can tolerate antimicrobials and is drug resistant. Can the biofilm be mutual benefit    (3)  
  or threat to community? Justify?  
  (1+2 = 3 marks)  
  
4B)   A small change in a molecule has led to the diverse functions. For this we need to examine            (3)  
  molecules such as haemoglobin, myoglobin, hemocyanin, leghaemoglobin and chlorophyll. All  
  of them are modified porphyrins.  
  (i) What is the central metal ion coordinated to Porphyrin ring in case of Chlorophyll?  
  (ii) In case of hemocyanin crabs, octopus, snails, lobsters have blue blood, why?

(iii) What is the structural difference between Haemoglobin and Myoglobin?  
  (1+1+1 = 3 marks)  
  
4C)             Several attempts have been made from time to time to explain the origin of life on earth. As a  
  result, there are several theories which offer their own explanation on the possible mechanism of  
  origin of life. How can the justification given for the following theories, for origin of life?  
  (i) Theory of Special Creation  
  (ii) Theory of Spontaneous Generation                                                             (4)  
  (iii) Theory of Biogenesis  
  (iv) Theory of Biochemical Evolution  
  (1 mark × 4 = 4 marks)  
  
5A)             Give one example of living organisms which Bioinspired to create the following technology.  
  (i) Water Filters  
  (ii) Shock absorber                                                                               (3)  
  (iii) Bionic Car  
  
5B)             What does the following Symbols represent?  
  (i) +/0  
  (ii) +/-                                                                                          (3)  
  (iii) +/+  
  
5C)             (i) Vaccines can induce immunity. How is it possible?  
  (ii) Inactivated microorganism are used in the form of vaccines. Justify.  
  (iii) Is the booster shot required for all types of diseases?                                     (4)  
  (iv) How adjuvants have the capacity to increase effectiveness of vaccines?
